newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria far right soars in Euro-election.
newsitem.headline: Austria far right soars in Euro-election.

text.p: Support for the Social Democrats of Austrian Chancellor Franz Vranitzky slumped to an historic low in a European parliament election and the far right soared to an all-time high, computer projections showed.
The Social Democrats won 29.7 percent of the vote, the same as the conservative People's Party. Computer projections by Austrian state television showed the far-right Freedom Party at 28.1 percent.

Projections also showed the Social Democrats doing badly in a Vienna state election, losing its overall majority in Austria's richest and most powerful regional assembly for the first time since 1945.

The Euro-poll projections, if translated into final results, would spell a disaster for Vranitzky's Social Democrats, dealing the party its lowest nationwide score since democratic elections first took place in Austria in 1918.

For far-right Freedom Party leader Joerg Haider, the results will be hailed as a huge triumph and showed backing for his stand against the Maastricht treaty on European Union integration and a single currency. The result confirms Austria's far right as Europe's most successful nationalist grouping.

The conservative People's Party led by Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel, which fielded popular European parliament candidates, was expected to be pleased with a result putting it on a par with its government coalition partner.
